newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Baycorp sees better second half.
newsitem.headline: Baycorp sees better second half.

text.p: Baycorp Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it expected a "satisfactory" increase in net profit in the second half year over the same period last year.

Earlier, Baycorp reported a net profit of NZ$4 million for the six months to December 31, up from $3 million in the previous half year. It said the performance was in line with expected trading levels.

During the half year, the company's capital expenditure programme was well covered by its depreciation allowance. As in past periods, this allowed Baycorp to return most of the tax paid profit to shareholders in dividends.

"The task before the board now is to continue to consolidate the performance of its existing products while at the same time to develop new revenue producers based round the principal asset - the database," the company said.
"In this respect, shareholders may look forward to some interesting developments over the next 12 months which will have medium and longer term upside in improved trading results."
Baycorp said it continued to review expenditure, aiming to ensure maximum contribution from various operations.
It said as the company's revenue streams continued to increase, operating efficiencies ensured a constantly greater proportion of revenue flowed through to profitability.

Baycorp said it continued to focus on maximising tax paid returns to shareholders. It declared an interim fully imputed dividend of 10 NZ cents per share, up from seven cps in the previous corresponding period.
